ex: «Riverisco, signora contessa», disse il vecchio portiere togliendosi il cappello.
exEn: 'My respects, Countess,' said the old doorman, taking off his hat.
note: Dated, ceremonious (literally 'I revere you'); today heard only jokingly or among older speakers in Northern Italy. Cf. 'ossequi'.

ex: Si inchinò appena e mormorò «servo suo» prima di ritirarsi.
exEn: He bowed slightly and murmured 'your servant' before withdrawing.
note: Archaic formula, from 'sono servo suo'; now only ironic or in historical fiction. The Venetian equivalent 's-ciavo' gave rise to 'ciao'.

en: welcome (to someone who has just arrived)
ex: «Benarrivato, dottore! Il viaggio è stato lungo?»
exEn: 'Welcome, doctor! Was the journey long?'
note: Dated/regional; the neutral forms are 'benvenuto' and 'bentornato'. Agrees with the addressee: 'benarrivata', 'benarrivati'.

en: good to see you too (traditional reply to 'bentornato')
ex: «Bentornata, Lucia!» «Bentrovato, zio!»
exEn: 'Welcome back, Lucia!' 'Good to find you well, uncle!'
note: Slightly old-fashioned; the set answer to 'bentornato'. Agrees with the person addressed ('bentrovata', 'bentrovati').

ex: Porga i miei rispetti alla signora madre.
exEn: Please give my respects to your mother.
note: Formal, somewhat ceremonious; used at leave-taking or when sending regards. Near-synonyms: 'ossequi', 'i miei omaggi' (even more courtly).

en: exaggerated bows and greetings; obsequious pleasantries
ex: Dopo tanti salamelecchi il funzionario ci ha finalmente detto di no.
exEn: After all the bowing and scraping, the official finally told us no.
note: Colloquial and always ironic; from Arabic 'salam alaikum'. Used in the plural: 'fare salamelecchi'.

ex: Sbrigati i convenevoli, i due ministri passarono subito al dossier.
exEn: With the pleasantries out of the way, the two ministers went straight to the dossier.
note: Formal/literary, plural only in this sense; 'scambiarsi i convenevoli', 'senza tanti convenevoli'.

ex: Un cameriere compìto ci accompagnò al tavolo senza una parola di troppo.
exEn: A courteous waiter led us to our table without a single unnecessary word.
note: Literary; stressed on the i ('compìto'), unlike 'cómpito' (task). Near-synonyms: 'garbato' (neutral), 'urbano' (formal), 'ossequioso' (excessive).

ex: Le fece un baciamano perfetto, senza sfiorarle il guanto.
exEn: He gave her a perfect hand-kiss, without touching her glove.
note: Old-world etiquette: 'fare il baciamano a qualcuno'. Invariable in the plural (some dictionaries also admit 'baciamani').

ex: «Pregiatissimo Signor Direttore, mi permetto di sottoporLe la questione seguente.»
exEn: 'Most esteemed Director, allow me to submit the following matter to you.'
note: Epistolary/bureaucratic, abbreviated 'Preg.mo'. Ranks with 'Egregio', 'Illustrissimo' and 'Chiarissimo' (professors).

ex: La lettera era indirizzata all'Illustrissimo Signor Sindaco.
exEn: The letter was addressed to the Most Illustrious Mayor.
note: Formal address, abbreviated 'Ill.mo'; today often ironic. Historically also the title of nobles ('l'Illustrissimo').

ex: «Chiarissimo Professore, Le scrivo in merito alla mia tesi di dottorato.»
exEn: 'Distinguished Professor, I am writing to you regarding my doctoral thesis.'
note: Academic epistolary title, abbreviated 'Chiar.mo'; strictly for full professors ('ordinari'). Never used in speech.

ex: Il computo dei voti si è protratto fino all'alba.
exEn: The counting of the votes went on until dawn.
note: Formal/bureaucratic; 'computo metrico' is the bill of quantities in construction. Everyday synonym: 'conteggio'.

ex: Il disastro non fu che la sommatoria di tante piccole negligenze.
exEn: The disaster was nothing but the sum total of many small acts of negligence.
note: Technical (symbol Σ) and, by extension, formal for 'somma complessiva'.

ex: Il centimetro è un sottomultiplo del metro, come il milligrammo lo è del grammo.
exEn: The centimetre is a submultiple of the metre, as the milligram is of the gram.
note: Technical; opposite 'multiplo'. Also adjectival: 'unità sottomultiple'.

ex: Un numero frazionario si esprime come rapporto di due interi.
exEn: A fractional number is expressed as the ratio of two integers.
note: Technical; 'moneta frazionaria' = small change, 'riserva frazionaria' (banking).

ex: La diagonale del quadrato è incommensurabile con il lato, come scoprirono con sgomento i pitagorici.
exEn: The diagonal of a square is incommensurable with its side, as the Pythagoreans discovered to their dismay.
note: Precise mathematical sense (no common measure) and hyperbolic sense ('una distanza incommensurabile'). Noun 'incommensurabilità'.

ex: Ha ricostruito la vicenda con dovizia di particolari.
exEn: He reconstructed the affair with a wealth of detail.
note: Literary; virtually confined to the phrase 'con dovizia di particolari'. Adjective 'dovizioso'.

ex: I turisti arrivavano a frotte sul sagrato del duomo.
exEn: Tourists were arriving in droves on the cathedral square.
note: Mostly in 'a frotte' (in droves). Discriminate: 'stuolo' (orderly host), 'torma' (unruly band), 'turba' (mob).

ex: Una torma di ragazzini gli corse incontro chiedendo l'autografo.
exEn: A horde of kids ran up to him asking for an autograph.
note: Literary, faintly pejorative (Latin 'turma', a cavalry squadron). Cf. 'frotta', 'stuolo', 'turba'.

ex: La turba inferocita assediava il palazzo del governatore.
exEn: The enraged mob was besieging the governor's palace.
note: Literary and pejorative. In medicine 'turbe' means disturbances ('turbe psichiche', 'turbe del sonno').

ex: Il decreto è un coacervo di norme contraddittorie che nessuno sa applicare.
exEn: The decree is a jumble of contradictory rules that nobody knows how to apply.
note: Learned (Latin 'coacervus'), usually pejorative. In inheritance law 'coacervo' is the notional reunion of assets.

ex: Una fiumana di gente sfilava lungo i viali verso lo stadio.
exEn: A flood of people was streaming along the avenues towards the stadium.
note: Literary; also literal ('la fiumana travolse il ponte'). Cf. 'marea di gente' (neutral).

ex: Le sedie erano in soprannumero e le hanno accatastate in corridoio.
exEn: There were more chairs than needed and they were stacked in the corridor.
note: Bureaucratic; 'personale in soprannumero' = surplus staff. Adjective 'soprannumerario'.

ex: Mettici solo uno zinzino di sale, altrimenti copre il sapore del pesce.
exEn: Put in just a smidgen of salt, otherwise it hides the flavour of the fish.
note: Regional (Tuscany and Centre), colloquial; also 'un zinzino'. Neutral equivalents: 'un pizzico', 'un briciolo'.

ex: C'era uno sfracello di gente e non siamo nemmeno riusciti a entrare.
exEn: There was a massive crowd and we couldn't even get in.
note: Colloquial hyperbole ('uno sfracello di soldi'); literal sense 'fare uno sfracello' = to smash to pieces.

ex: La soprano fu accolta da un subisso di applausi.
exEn: The soprano was greeted by a thunder of applause.
note: Literary, from 'subissare' (to overwhelm); typically 'un subisso di applausi/fischi/domande'.

ex: Con quel brevetto ha fatto soldi a palate.
exEn: With that patent he made money hand over fist.
note: Colloquial (from 'palata', shovelful); mainly with 'soldi'. Cf. 'a iosa', 'a bizzeffe'.

ex: Il giudice ha riconosciuto il danno ma deve ancora stabilirne il quantum.
exEn: The judge has recognised the damage but has yet to determine the amount.
note: Latinism, legal and economic ('an e quantum debeatur'); in physics the plural is 'quanti'.

ex: Il bambino è al novantesimo percentile per altezza e al cinquantesimo per peso.
exEn: The child is at the 90th percentile for height and the 50th for weight.
note: Statistical; common in paediatrics and test scores.

ex: I bottoni si vendevano a grosse, cioè a dozzine di dozzine.
exEn: Buttons used to be sold by the gross, that is, by dozens of dozens.
note: Historical commercial unit; do not confuse with the adjective 'grossa' or 'una grossa' (a big one).

ex: Ha vinto un ambo sulla ruota di Napoli giocando i numeri della nonna.
exEn: He won a two-number combination on the Naples wheel playing his grandmother's numbers.
note: Lotto series: ambo, terno, quaterna, cinquina. Also archaic adjective 'ambo le mani' (both hands).

ex: Il duomo di Siena è un unicum nel panorama del gotico italiano.
exEn: Siena cathedral is a one-off in the panorama of Italian Gothic.
note: Latinism, learned; the Latin plural 'unica' is rare. Cf. 'un caso a sé'.

ex: Un calcolo spannometrico ci dice che servono almeno tre giorni.
exEn: A back-of-the-envelope calculation tells us it will take at least three days.
note: Jocular colloquialism coined on 'spanna' (hand-span) + '-metrico'; cf. 'a spanne', 'a occhio e croce'.

ex: Un tramonto porporino incendiava il cielo sopra la laguna.
exEn: A crimson-purple sunset set the sky over the lagoon ablaze.
note: Literary; 'porpora' is the noun (also the cardinal's rank). Cf. 'purpureo' (more solemn), 'cremisi'.

ex: Le labbra dipinte di carminio spiccavano sul viso pallidissimo.
exEn: Her carmine-painted lips stood out against her very pale face.
note: Art and cosmetics; also invariable adjective ('rosso carminio'). Historically extracted from cochineal.

ex: Il pittore rese l'incarnato della modella con sottili velature rosate.
exEn: The painter rendered the model's flesh tones with subtle pinkish glazes.
note: Art-historical and literary; 'incarnato di pesca'. As adjective: 'rosa incarnato'.

ex: Un vecchio canuto sedeva ogni mattina sulla panchina davanti alla chiesa.
exEn: A white-haired old man sat every morning on the bench in front of the church.
note: Literary; noun 'canizie' (white hair, old age). Neutral: 'con i capelli bianchi'; 'brizzolato' = greying.

ex: Un cielo bigio prometteva pioggia per tutto il giorno.
exEn: A drab grey sky promised rain for the whole day.
note: Tuscan/literary; 'né bianco né bigio' = neither one thing nor the other. Cf. 'grigio' (neutral), 'cinereo', 'plumbeo'.

ex: Ha scelto tende di lino ecrù per la camera degli ospiti.
exEn: She chose ecru linen curtains for the guest room.
note: Invariable; textile term from French 'écru'. Also spelt 'écru'.

ex: Il disegno è eseguito a penna e bistro su carta avorio.
exEn: The drawing is executed in pen and bistre on ivory paper.
note: Art term; also invariable adjective ('bruno bistro'). Not the French café, which in Italian is 'bistrot'.

ex: Indossava un abito pervinca che le illuminava gli occhi.
exEn: She wore a periwinkle-blue dress that lit up her eyes.
note: Invariable colour adjective ('blu pervinca'); as feminine noun it is the plant.

ex: Le statue di bronzo del giardino erano coperte di verderame.
exEn: The bronze statues in the garden were covered in verdigris.
note: Also the copper-based fungicide sprayed on vines; adjective use 'verde verderame'.

ex: Ha dipinto la parete del soggiorno di un ottanio profondo.
exEn: She painted the living-room wall a deep teal.
note: Invariable; fashion and interior-design term ('blu ottanio', 'verde ottanio'). Near-synonym 'petrolio'.

ex: Portava una sciarpa vinaccia su un cappotto grigio ferro.
exEn: He wore a dark wine-red scarf over an iron-grey coat.
note: Invariable as colour ('color vinaccia'); as feminine noun 'le vinacce' are the pressed grape skins distilled into grappa.

ex: I tifosi granata invasero la piazza dopo il derby.
exEn: The garnet-red (Torino) fans flooded the square after the derby.
note: Invariable; 'granata' is the emblematic colour of Torino FC. Homonyms: pomegranate, hand grenade.

ex: Nella stagione aurea del Rinascimento Firenze dettava il gusto all'Europa.
exEn: In the golden age of the Renaissance, Florence dictated taste to Europe.
note: Literary; 'sezione aurea' (golden ratio), 'aurea mediocritas'. Literal 'gold-coloured' is 'dorato'.

ex: Una luce argentea filtrava tra le nuvole sul mare.
exEn: A silvery light filtered through the clouds over the sea.
note: Literary; distinguish from 'argentato' (silver-plated) and 'argentino' (silvery in sound).

ex: Un cielo ferrigno pesava sulla pianura gelata.
exEn: An iron-grey sky weighed on the frozen plain.
note: Literary; also of character or bodies ('una tempra ferrigna').

ex: L'acciaio brunito della canna non rifletteva la luce.
exEn: The burnished steel of the barrel did not reflect the light.
note: Technical (gunsmithing, goldsmithing: 'brunitura'); literary for dark gleaming surfaces.

ex: Una mucca pezzata pascolava vicino al torrente.
exEn: A piebald cow was grazing near the stream.
note: Zootechnical ('pezzata rossa' is a cattle breed); 'pezzatura' = pattern of patches. Cf. 'maculato', 'screziato'.

ex: Le vetrate policrome inondano la navata di luce colorata.
exEn: The polychrome stained-glass windows flood the nave with coloured light.
note: Art-historical; stress 'polìcromo'. Opposite 'monocromo'. Noun 'policromia'.

ex: I muri fuligginosi della vecchia stazione raccontavano un secolo di locomotive a vapore.
exEn: The sooty walls of the old station told of a century of steam locomotives.
note: Literary; from 'fuliggine' (soot). Cf. 'nerastro', 'cinereo'.

ex: La testa ovoidale delle figure di Modigliani è inconfondibile.
exEn: The egg-shaped heads of Modigliani's figures are unmistakable.
note: Technical/art term for three-dimensional shapes; 'ovale' is the flat figure.

ex: Le tavolette d'argilla recavano iscrizioni cuneiformi.
exEn: The clay tablets bore cuneiform inscriptions.
note: Learned (Latin 'cuneus', wedge); also anatomical ('ossa cuneiformi').

ex: Le foglie fusiformi dell'oleandro resistono bene alla siccità.
exEn: The spindle-shaped leaves of the oleander withstand drought well.
note: Botanical/anatomical; from 'fuso' (spindle). Cf. 'affusolato' (tapered, of fingers).

ex: Una nube lenticolare, immobile sopra la vetta, annunciava vento in quota.
exEn: A lenticular cloud, motionless above the summit, announced wind at altitude.
note: Technical (meteorology, optics, galaxies); from 'lenticchia'.

ex: Le mura ciclopiche di Alatri sono fatte di blocchi incastrati senza malta.
exEn: The cyclopean walls of Alatri are made of blocks fitted together without mortar.
note: Archaeological term for huge polygonal masonry; figuratively 'uno sforzo ciclopico'. Cf. 'immane', 'mastodontico'.

ex: Serviva le portate su piattini lillipuziani, con porzioni da nouvelle cuisine.
exEn: She served the courses on Lilliputian little plates, with nouvelle-cuisine portions.
note: Learned/jocular, from Swift's Lilliput; opposite 'gargantuesco', 'ciclopico'.

ex: Si avvolse nella gabbana e uscì nella tormenta.
exEn: He wrapped himself in his greatcoat and went out into the blizzard.
note: Dated/regional; survives mainly in 'voltagabbana' (turncoat) and 'voltare gabbana'.

ex: Il pastrano militare del nonno pesava come una coperta di lana.
exEn: Grandfather's army greatcoat weighed as much as a wool blanket.
note: Dated/literary; 'cappotto' is the neutral word. Cf. 'tabarro' (cloak), 'paltò' (regional).

ex: Sotto la redingote portava un panciotto di seta a fiori.
exEn: Under his frock coat he wore a flowered silk waistcoat.
note: French loan (from English 'riding coat'), invariable; 19th-century menswear, today a fitted women's coat.

ex: Lo sposo indossava un tight grigio perla con il cilindro.
exEn: The groom wore a pearl-grey morning suit with a top hat.
note: False friend: in Italian 'tight' is the morning coat, never tights ('collant'). Invariable, pronounced 'tait'.

ex: Il gondoliere in costume settecentesco portava un tricorno nero.
exEn: The gondolier in eighteenth-century costume wore a black tricorn.
note: Historical; associated with Goldoni's Venice and the carabinieri's dress uniform ('la lucerna').

ex: Le donne entravano in chiesa con la mantiglia di pizzo nero sul capo.
exEn: The women entered the church with black lace mantillas on their heads.
note: From Spanish; Southern and ceremonial usage. Cf. 'velo', 'scialle'.

ex: Teneva le mani nel manicotto di pelliccia, come una dama d'altri tempi.
exEn: She kept her hands in a fur muff, like a lady of bygone days.
note: Also technical: pipe coupling, insulating sleeve. The pasta 'manicotti' is Italian-American.

ex: Un abito da sera in crespo di seta nero, senza un ornamento.
exEn: A black silk crêpe evening dress, without a single ornament.
note: Textile term ('crespo di Cina'); as adjective 'crespo' = frizzy ('capelli crespi').

ex: Portava pantaloni di fustagno da lavoro e una giacca di velluto a coste.
exEn: He wore work trousers of fustian and a corduroy jacket.
note: Traditional workwear fabric, named after Fustat (Cairo).

ex: Una giacca di tweed spigato, con le toppe ai gomiti.
exEn: A herringbone tweed jacket with elbow patches.
note: Tailoring; also noun 'lo spigato'. Everyday equivalent 'a spina di pesce'.

ex: I gomiti lisi della giacca tradivano anni passati alla scrivania.
exEn: The threadbare elbows of his jacket betrayed years spent at a desk.
note: Literary/formal; cf. 'logoro' (worn out, also figurative), 'frusto', 'consunto'.

ex: Un cappotto frusto e sformato gli pendeva dalle spalle.
exEn: A worn-out, shapeless coat hung from his shoulders.
note: Literary; figurative use is common ('un'espressione frusta' = a hackneyed phrase). Do not confuse with 'frusta' (whip).

ex: Con i pantaloni sdruciti e le scarpe rotte, sembrava un vagabondo.
exEn: With his ripped trousers and broken shoes, he looked like a tramp.
note: Literary; from 'sdrucire' (to unstitch). Cf. 'sbrindellato', 'cencioso', 'stracciato' (neutral).

ex: Infagottata in tre maglioni, uscì a spalare la neve.
exEn: Bundled up in three jumpers, she went out to shovel snow.
note: Colloquial/expressive, from 'fagotto' (bundle); implies shapelessness. Cf. 'imbacuccato' (wrapped up warm).

ex: Una giacca sciancrata che segnava la vita e allungava la figura.
exEn: A waisted jacket that defined the waist and lengthened the figure.
note: Tailoring term (from 'anca'); noun 'sciancratura'. Opposite 'diritto', 'a sacco'.

ex: Le tende erano rifinite con una passamaneria dorata da teatro.
exEn: The curtains were finished with a gilt theatrical braid trim.
note: Craft term covering cords, fringes, tassels, galloons; also the shop that sells them.

ex: Un cappotto blu con gli alamari di corda, come quello dei marinai.
exEn: A navy coat with rope frog fastenings, like the sailors' one.
note: Also the ornamental braid on uniforms; the Carabinieri's silver 'alamari' are their symbol.

ex: Il parroco indossava ancora la veste talare, come cinquant'anni fa.
exEn: The parish priest still wore the cassock, just as fifty years ago.
note: From Latin 'talus' (heel); almost only in 'veste/abito talare'. Cf. 'tonaca', 'saio' (friars).

ex: Nella Bohème il filosofo Colline canta l'addio alla sua vecchia zimarra.
exEn: In La Bohème the philosopher Colline sings a farewell to his old overcoat.
note: Dated/literary; historically a loose gown for men and clergy. Cf. 'palandrana'.

ex: La vedova, in gramaglie, seguiva il feretro a capo chino.
exEn: The widow, in mourning dress, followed the coffin with bowed head.
note: Literary, plural only: 'vestire in gramaglie', 'mettersi a gramaglie'. Neutral: 'a lutto'.

en: train (of a dress); aftermath, lingering consequence
ex: Due paggi reggevano lo strascico dell'abito nuziale lungo la navata.
exEn: Two page-boys carried the train of the wedding dress down the nave.
note: Figurative sense is very common: 'la vicenda ha lasciato strascichi giudiziari'. Also 'pesca a strascico' (trawling).

ex: La modista le provò tre cappellini prima di trovare quello giusto per le corse.
exEn: The milliner tried three little hats on her before finding the right one for the races.
note: Almost always feminine (plural 'modiste'); a man is 'un modista' (plural 'modisti'). Not 'fashion designer' ('stilista').

ex: Un monile d'oro etrusco brillava nella teca del museo.
exEn: An Etruscan gold necklace gleamed in the museum case.
note: Literary/archaeological; everyday 'gioiello', 'collana'.

ex: Guadarono il fiume con l'acqua fino alla cintola.
exEn: They forded the river with the water up to their waists.
note: Dated/literary; survives in 'fino alla cintola', 'nudo fino alla cintola'. Neutral: 'cintura', 'vita'.

ex: Portava lo zaino a bandoliera, con una sola cinghia sul petto.
exEn: He carried the rucksack bandolier-style, with a single strap across his chest.
note: Feminine noun; the phrase 'a bandoliera' (diagonally across the chest) is the living use.

en: pro rata; in proportion to time or share
ex: Gli interessi maturano pro rata temporis, giorno per giorno.
exEn: Interest accrues pro rata temporis, day by day.
note: Latinism of law and accounting; often with 'temporis'. Adjective/noun 'pro rata' also in 'il prorata IVA'.

ex: Le spese straordinarie si ripartiscono pro quota tra i condòmini.
exEn: Extraordinary expenses are divided among the co-owners in proportion to their shares.
note: Latinism, legal/administrative register; cf. 'pro rata' (by time), 'pro capite' (per head).

en: emphyteusis (long lease of land with duty to improve)
ex: Il terreno era gravato da un'enfiteusi risalente al Settecento.
exEn: The land was encumbered by an emphyteutic lease dating back to the eighteenth century.
note: Juridical (Civil Code, art. 957 ff.); the holder is the 'enfiteuta', the owner the 'concedente'. Invariable.

ex: Con la surroga abbiamo trasferito il mutuo a una banca con un tasso migliore.
exEn: Through a subrogation we transferred the mortgage to a bank with a better rate.
note: Banking/legal; also 'surrogazione'. In politics 'surroga' is the replacement of a resigned member.

ex: Le parti hanno convenuto una novazione del contratto originario.
exEn: The parties agreed on a novation of the original contract.
note: Strictly juridical (art. 1230 c.c.); do not confuse with 'innovazione'.

en: compounding of interest (charging interest on interest)
ex: La Cassazione ha dichiarato illegittimo l'anatocismo bancario trimestrale.
exEn: The Supreme Court declared quarterly bank compounding of interest unlawful.
note: Juridical/financial Greek-derived term; 'interessi anatocistici'.

ex: Il referendum del 1985 abrogò il meccanismo della scala mobile.
exEn: The 1985 referendum abolished the wage-indexation mechanism.
note: In economic history the automatic link between wages and inflation (1945-1992); the everyday meaning is 'escalator'.

ex: Firmò un pagherò a novanta giorni per saldare la fornitura.
exEn: He signed a ninety-day promissory note to settle the supply.
note: Commercial law ('pagherò cambiario'); invariable, from 'io pagherò'. Cf. 'cambiale', 'tratta'.

ex: La banca ha ridotto il castelletto dell'azienda da centomila a cinquantamila euro.
exEn: The bank cut the company's discount facility from one hundred thousand to fifty thousand euros.
note: Banking jargon; literally 'little castle'. Cf. 'fido' (general credit line).

ex: Gli incagli sono cresciuti più delle sofferenze nel bilancio della banca.
exEn: Unlikely-to-pay loans grew faster than bad loans in the bank's accounts.
note: Banking classification ('crediti incagliati', between 'in bonis' and 'in sofferenza'); nautical sense = grounding.

ex: I creditori chirografari vengono soddisfatti solo dopo quelli privilegiati.
exEn: Unsecured creditors are paid only after the secured ones.
note: Bankruptcy law; from Greek 'cheirographon' (handwritten document). Opposite 'privilegiato', 'ipotecario'.

en: fictitious foreign residence (of a company, to evade tax)
ex: La Guardia di Finanza contesta al gruppo un'esterovestizione durata dieci anni.
exEn: The tax police accuse the group of a ten-year fictitious foreign residence.
note: Tax-law neologism ('vestire da estero'); typical of financial journalism.

en: voluntary correction of a tax return with reduced penalties
ex: Ha regolarizzato la posizione con il ravvedimento operoso, pagando una sanzione ridotta.
exEn: He regularised his position through voluntary correction, paying a reduced penalty.
note: Italian tax-law institution; 'ravvedimento' alone is literary for 'repentance'.

ex: Nei racconti popolari il gabelliere è sempre avido e odiato.
exEn: In folk tales the tax collector is always greedy and hated.
note: From 'gabella' (duty); today only historical or contemptuous. Cf. 'esattore' (neutral).

en: quota system; rationing of imports or supplies
ex: Il contingentamento delle importazioni di acciaio ha scatenato una guerra commerciale.
exEn: The quota system on steel imports triggered a trade war.
note: Trade-policy term, from 'contingente' (quota); verb 'contingentare'.

ex: Il signoraggio della banca centrale è un tema caro ai teorici del complotto.
exEn: Central-bank seigniorage is a favourite topic of conspiracy theorists.
note: Monetary economics; historically the lord's right to mint coins.

ex: «Resilienza» è una parola di nuovo conio entrata ovunque.
exEn: 'Resilience' is a newly coined word that has got in everywhere.
note: Literal (die for minting) and figurative: 'di nuovo conio' (newly coined), 'dello stesso conio' (of the same ilk).

ex: Nel 1866 il governo decretò il corso forzoso della lira, sospendendo la convertibilità in oro.
exEn: In 1866 the government decreed forced currency for the lira, suspending gold convertibility.
note: Monetary history; cf. 'corso legale' (legal tender).

ex: L'aggio del tabaccaio sui valori bollati è di pochi punti percentuali.
exEn: The tobacconist's commission on revenue stamps is a few percentage points.
note: Commercial/financial; 'aggio di emissione'. Opposite 'disaggio'. Not related to 'agio' (ease).

ex: L'immobile è iscritto a bilancio tra i cespiti ammortizzabili.
exEn: The building is entered in the accounts among the depreciable assets.
note: Accounting/legal; from Latin 'caespes' (turf). 'Registro dei cespiti' = fixed-asset register.

ex: I tre soci fondatori hanno stretto un patto parasociale sul diritto di voto.
exEn: The three founding partners entered into a shareholders' agreement on voting rights.
note: Company law (art. 2341-bis c.c.); binds the parties but not the company itself.

en: shell company in a chain of holdings; Chinese box
ex: Il gruppo controllava la fabbrica attraverso una catena di scatole cinesi.
exEn: The group controlled the factory through a chain of nested holding companies.
note: Financial-journalism metaphor for pyramidal holdings; literally nested boxes.

ex: Nel mercato dei braccianti stagionali la grande distribuzione agisce quasi come un monopsonio.
exEn: In the seasonal farm-labour market, large retailers act almost as a monopsony.
note: Economics; mirror image of 'monopolio'. Adjective 'monopsonistico'.

ex: L'antico opificio tessile è diventato un museo di archeologia industriale.
exEn: The old textile works has become a museum of industrial archaeology.
note: Formal/dated ('Opificio delle Pietre Dure' in Florence); neutral 'fabbrica', 'stabilimento'.

ex: Le filande della Brianza impiegavano soprattutto donne e bambine.
exEn: The silk mills of Brianza employed mainly women and girls.
note: Economic and social history of Northern Italy; the worker was a 'filandera' (regional).

ex: La partita doppia fu codificata da Luca Pacioli nel 1494.
exEn: Double-entry bookkeeping was codified by Luca Pacioli in 1494.
note: Accounting; 'tenere la contabilità in partita doppia'.

ex: Il commercialista ha ricostruito i movimenti sospetti dal libro mastro.
exEn: The accountant reconstructed the suspicious transactions from the general ledger.
note: Accounting; often just 'il mastro'. Cf. 'libro giornale' (journal), 'prima nota' (daybook).

ex: L'Italia ha mantenuto un avanzo primario per quasi tutti gli anni Duemila.
exEn: Italy maintained a primary surplus for almost all of the 2000s.
note: Public finance; opposite 'disavanzo primario'.

ex: La vedova percepisce la pensione di reversibilità del marito.
exEn: The widow receives her husband's survivor's pension.
note: Welfare law ('pensione di reversibilità'); in science 'reversibilità di una reazione'.

ex: Prima dell'annuncio qualcuno aveva fatto incetta di azioni della società.
exEn: Before the announcement someone had bought up shares in the company.
note: Fixed collocation 'fare incetta di'; can be neutral or imply speculation.
